what: What DSP 3.0.13 puts on the line for ATA, generated inside the emulator by the C52 firmware
image: IDSDL302.ROM (supervisor + DSP 3.0.13, 20.16 MHz), booted through the captured on-chip ROM
sample_rate_basis: the DSP's dial-path codec rate (docs/codec-rate-312.md), the same basis as artifacts/dtmf-emulator-302-01

bursts.identification: V.8 ANSam: 2100 Hz answer tone with 15.05 Hz amplitude modulation
bursts.basis: carrier measured 2101.15 Hz here and 2098.90 Hz in the --exchange-hotline run, i.e. within 1.2 Hz of 2100 either way; the AM sidebands pull a finite-window peak search slightly, so treat the carrier as 2100 +/- 1.5 Hz rather than the printed decimals. First-order sidebands at +/-15.05 Hz near 10%, second-order near 1%; matches the 3.1.2 firmware-rendered ANSam in artifacts/answer-tone-01 (0.101/0.100)

bursts.identification: consistent with V.22/V.22bis unscrambled binary 1 (channel 2 carrier 2400 Hz less 150 Hz)
bursts.basis: measured 2250.00 Hz with no modulation sidebands. This is a match against the standard, NOT a firmware attribution: the 3.0.13 code that arms it has not been located

reproduced: the same sequence appears with --exchange-hotline in place of --ring, at the same onsets, durations and levels; the 2250 Hz burst is byte-identical between the two runs
caveats: The harness tone generator was deleted before these runs (commit 797ed28), so only the C52 program could have produced these samples; the codec, ASIC transport and line remain models.

Neither run is a true exchange-side answer. The CLI's --ring drives the ring detector at port 0x14 but never puts LineExchange into 'ringing' - only the SIP inbound path calls exchange.ring() - so bridge.set_line_hook labels the seizure 'originate'. The supervisor obeyed ATA and armed these tones regardless.
The 3.0.13 oscillator addresses are unlocated. The 3.1.2 answer-tone family (874f/8739/8712, docs/answer-tone.md) does not transplant: none of those addresses hold the same words in this image.
